name: Verification expressions
purpose: The cve table holds the checks that make up the criteria of parameter-based verification stages: one record per check, naming a monitoring parameter, the expected value, a tolerance and the representation (raw, engineering, or echo of a command parameter value). All checks of the same stage are ANDed. The ICD recommends taking all verification parameters of a stage from the same telemetry packet (see CVS_SPID). Parameter validity is taken into account automatically: a check passes only if the parameter is valid and its value meets the criterion. The table has a second role: it identifies the monitoring parameters affected by a command, so that their status consistency checking (PCF_USCON) is suspended during the verification window and, at the end, the expected value is updated. For status-consistency-checked parameters the check must use the same raw or engineering form (CVE_INTER) as the parameter's out-of-limits checks (OCF_INTER), and all cve records for the same parameter must use the same representation, across all stages.

fields.name: CVE_CVSID
fields.description: Identifier (CVS_ID) of the verification stage this check belongs to. Only parameter-based stages (CVS_SOURCE = 'V') are allowed. Part of the key.

fields.name: CVE_PARNAM
fields.description: Name of an existing monitoring parameter (PCF_NAME) used for the check. Restrictions: its raw representation must be numerical (no strings or times), and it must be processed by the telemetry model, that is, a TM parameter in plf or a synthetic parameter of any type. If the parameter is subject to status consistency checking (PCF_USCON = 'Y'), the representation of the verification value (CVE_INTER) must match that of its OOL checks (OCF_INTER). Part of the key, so a parameter can appear only once per stage.

fields.name: CVE_INTER
fields.description: Representation of the expected value CVE_VAL and tolerance CVE_TOL. If one monitoring parameter appears in several parameter-based stages, 'E' is only allowed if every one of its cve records uses 'E': records with 'R' or 'C' and records with 'E' cannot be mixed for the same parameter.

values.meaning: Raw values. For synthetic parameters the raw value is the source value produced by the OL or hard-coded definition
Engineering (calibrated) values. Only for parameters with one or more calibration definitions (see PCF_CURTX)
Echo check: CVE_VAL is the name of a command parameter; CVE_TOL is then always raw, so a status-consistency-checked verification parameter must be checked raw (OCF_INTER = 'U')

fields.name: CVE_VAL
fields.description: Value the verification parameter is compared with. It uses raw form unless CVE_INTER = 'E'. Raw values are decimal, in a format compatible with the parameter type (PCF_PTC). Engineering values follow the parameter's engineering representation: ASCII text for status parameters (PCF_CATEG = 'S') or the CAF_ENGFMT of the numerical calibration. For echo verification (CVE_INTER = 'C'), the field holds the name of a command parameter (CDF_PNAME) whose value at command instantiation is the reference. That parameter should appear only once in the command; if it appears more than once, the first instance is used. The field is only applicable, and then cannot be Null, when CVE_CHECK = 'B'; it is not used when CVE_CHECK = 'S'.

fields.name: CVE_TOL
fields.description: Allowed tolerance: the check passes when CVE_PARNAM lies within CVE_VAL plus or minus CVE_TOL. It is expressed in the same representation and format rules as CVE_VAL. It must be Null when an engineering representation (CVE_INTER = 'E') is used for a status parameter (PCF_CATEG = 'S').

fields.name: CVE_CHECK
fields.description: Controls whether the check drives only the status consistency checking of the verification parameter or also the actual command verification.

values.meaning: Both: used for verification and to disable and then re-enable status consistency checking of CVE_PARNAM (if it is status-consistency checked); CVE_VAL becomes the new expected value at the end of the stage window
Status consistency only: used just to disable status consistency checking of CVE_PARNAM. Allowed only together with at least one other check with CVE_CHECK = 'B' in the same stage

relationships.note: Numeric-raw, TM-model parameter. Its PCF_USCON, PCF_CATEG, PCF_CURTX and PCF_PTC constrain CVE_INTER, CVE_VAL and CVE_TOL.
For status-consistency-checked parameters CVE_INTER must match OCF_INTER. ocf says OCF_CODIN must be compatible with CVE_INTER when the parameter is used in cve (§3.3.2.3.1, PDF p.74).
Echo verification (CVE_INTER = 'C'): command parameter whose instantiated value is the reference.

history: ICD 5.1 §3.3.3.4.2 (icd-5-1-tos-gci, PDF p.94-96) has the same 6 fields, with CVE_CVSID Number(5). The differences are in the text. In 5.1 any TM or synthetic parameter with a numerical raw value is allowed, 'E' requires PCF_CURTX not Null (a single calibration curve), and the introduction requires OCF_INTER = 'C' when CVE_INTER = 'E' and advises against status consistency checking of echo-verified parameters. ICD 6.0 added 'describe constraint in the use of parameter views in the CVE table' (Annex 1 item 6, PDF p.244), giving the same-representation rules. ICD 6.4 restricted CVE_PARNAM, like other TM references, to parameters processed by the TM model (PDF p.254). ICD 6.7 Draft A prints CVE_CVSID as Number(10) (icd-6-7-drafta PDF p.182). ICD 6.9 changed it back to Number(5) to match CVS_ID (S2K-DCR-3909, PDF p.260; tracked change visible in icd-6-9-archive-org PDF p.187). ICD 7.0 (PDF p.194-199) keeps Number(5). Not modelled in pyscos2000 (7.2).
notes: Column mapping: COL1..COL6 = CVE_CVSID, CVE_PARNAM, CVE_INTER, CVE_VAL, CVE_TOL, CVE_CHECK; all 171 lines of the 2025 cve.dat have 6 fields. Consistency with ICD 7.0: every CVE_CVSID refers to a cvs stage with CVS_SOURCE = 'V', every 'V' stage has at least one check (167 stages, 171 checks; stages 9082-9085 have two ANDed checks each), and every CVE_PARNAM exists in pcf. CVE_INTER is 'R' in 81 rows and 'E' in 90. There is no echo verification ('C'), and CVE_CHECK is always 'B'. All 90 'E' checks use status parameters (PCF_CATEG = 'S', textual calibration) with text values such as ENABLED/DISABLED, On/Off, IMAGE_0/IMAGE_1, and CVE_TOL empty, as the ICD requires. No parameter used in cve has PCF_USCON = 'Y'. Release difference: in 2025, 78 'R' rows have CVE_TOL = '0', whereas the same rows have an empty tolerance in the 2020-04-16 release. This is the only change in cve between the releases. The SWA IDB cve.dat is empty. pyscos2000 has no cve model.
